---
id: "smk-20"
title: "Lisp (programming language)"
---

Lisp is a family of programming languages with a long history and a distinctive parenthesised prefix notation. It was specified by John McCarthy in 1958 at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, originally as a mathematical notation for computer programs, and it is the second-oldest high-level language still in widespread use after Fortran. Lisp introduced many ideas that later became common, including tree data structures, automatic storage management, dynamic typing, conditionals, higher-order functions and the read-eval-print loop. Code and data share the same list structure, which makes it possible to write macros that transform programs. The most widely used dialects today are Common Lisp, Scheme, Racket, Clojure and Emacs Lisp. Lisp was closely associated with artificial intelligence research for decades, and it remains popular for its flexibility and its interactive style of development.
